memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then they said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Now let us take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the Lord our God, or he may strike us with plagues or with the sword."" - Exodus 5:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses and Aaron do not argue theology with Pharaoh. They simply say: the God of the Hebrews has met with us.

That is testimony. Not an argument, not a clever defence — just a report of what happened. It is the same thing the man born blind said when religious leaders tried to trap him: one thing I know, I was blind and now I see (Jn 9:25). You cannot easily debate someone's experience of God.

Notice also the humility in their words. They speak of God striking them, not Pharaoh. They are not using God as a weapon against an enemy. They speak as people under God's authority themselves.

That matters. When we speak about God to others, there is always a temptation to sound superior — as though we are the ones who have got it right. The truth is that we stand under the same holiness we are describing.

Speak simply. Speak humbly. Tell people what God has done, and let Him do the convincing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did I last simply tell someone what God has done in my life?
2. Do I speak about God as one who stands over others, or beside them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me courage to speak of You simply and humbly. Let my testimony point to You and not to myself. Amen.
